history.origins: Originated in Finland; SÃ¶kÃ¶ is the Finnish word for 'Check' (in the poker sense) or potentially derived from a Swedish word. Despite the name 'Canadian Stud', it is most strongly associated with Finland and widely played there.
timeline: Present: A staple of Finnish poker culture and online poker sites focused on the Nordic market.
history.cultural: Very popular in Finland; often played as a pot-limit game.
history.evolution: Standard Five Card Stud adapted with four-card hands to liven up the gameplay.

setup.dealing: Standard Five Card Stud deal: Everyone antes. Each player receives one card face down (hole) and one card face up (door).

rules.objective: Win the pot with the best hand according to SÃ¶kÃ¶ rankings, or by bluffing.
rules.gameplay: 1. Ante. 2. Deal 1 down, 1 up. 3. Bring-in (forced bet by lowest/highest card) and betting round. 4. Deal 3rd street (face up), betting. 5. Fourth street (face up), betting. 6. Fifth street (face up), betting. 7. Showdown.
keyRules: Five Card Stud structure (1 down, 4 up)

strategy.basic: Starting hand selection is critical. A pair, a 4-flush draw, or 4-straight draw are playable. High cards are valuable. With the extra rankings, draws are more powerful than in regular Stud.
strategy.intermediate: Recognize that a 4-flush or 4-straight is often a winning hand against a single pair. However, Two Pair is still a very strong hand. Bluffing opportunities increase because a board showing 3 flush cards represents a likely 4-flush (a made hand).
strategy.advanced: Pot odds calculation must include the 4-card outs. Semi-bluffing with 3-card flush/straight draws on 3rd street is viable. Read the opponent's board: if they can't have a 4-card hand or pair, aggressive betting is key.
tips: Don't undervalue Four-Card Straights/Flushes; they beat One Pair.
